package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to 3.0.5.RELEASE (3.x), all versions prior to 2.4.4.RELEASE (1.x, 2.x)
package_info.why_malicious: The package fails to restrict XML External Entity (XXE) processing in its XML parsing utilities, allowing attackers to inject malicious XML that can exfiltrate sensitive data, perform server-side request forgery (SSRF), or access internal resources. This vulnerability enables attackers to exploit insecure XML parser configurations to compromise confidentiality and integrity.

execution_context.file_location: Any code path in spring-ws-core or spring-xml that uses DocumentBuilderFactory, XMLInputFactory, or similar XML parsing utilities without secure configuration
required_permissions: filesystem (to read files referenced by external entities)
network (if external entities reference remote resources or URLs)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the application parses user-supplied XML input, the XML parser processes a crafted XML document containing an external entity reference, causing the parser to read the contents of /etc/passwd and include this data in the application's XML processing output, resulting in potential data exfiltration to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows external entity resolution in XML parsing, which can be exploited to read arbitrary files from the server or initiate network requests to attacker-controlled endpoints. This behavior is a hallmark of XXE vulnerabilities and can lead to data leakage or SSRF.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure XML parsing should disable external entity resolution and DTD processing for untrusted input. The actual behavior allows attackers to inject DTDs and access sensitive files or internal network resources, violating the principle of least privilege and secure input handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of external entities is rare and typically only occurs in trusted, internal XML workflows where both the XML source and the referenced resources are fully controlled and validated. In public-facing or user-supplied XML processing, such behavior is almost never justified.
key_indicators: Presence of <!DOCTYPE ... [ <!ENTITY ... SYSTEM ...> ]> in incoming XML payloads
Use of XML parser factories (e.g., DocumentBuilderFactory, XMLInputFactory) without disabling external entity resolution or DTD processing
Unexpected access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ) or outbound network requests during XML parsing
Application responses or logs containing contents of files referenced in XML entities

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a malicious XML payload containing a crafted external entity reference (e.g., referencing /etc/passwd or a remote URL).
attack_chain.leads_to: The XML parser receives and begins processing the malicious XML input.

attack_chain.action: The XML parser, due to insecure configuration, resolves the external entity, reading the contents of the referenced file or initiating a network request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is extracted from the server or a network request is made to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

attack_chain.action: The application includes the resolved entity's data in its XML processing output, which may be returned in an API response or otherwise exposed to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive server data or confirms SSRF capability.

behavioral_signatures: XML parsing of untrusted input with external entity resolution or DTD processing enabled
Unexpected file access (e.g., /etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ) during XML parsing operations
Outbound DNS or HTTP requests triggered during XML parsing, especially to domains not normally contacted by the application
Presence of <!DOCTYPE> and <!ENTITY ... SYSTEM ...> in XML payloads received by the application
file_indicators: XML files or payloads containing DOCTYPE and ENTITY definitions, especially with SYSTEM or PUBLIC identifiers
Application logs showing access to sensitive files during XML processing
References to sensitive file paths (e.g., /etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ, C:\Windows\win.ini) in XML input
network_indicators: Outbound requests to attacker-controlled domains or IPs during XML parsing
Unexpected DNS lookups or HTTP requests initiated by the application in response to XML input
Network traffic to uncommon ports or protocols during XML processing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor XML parsing code for use of DocumentBuilderFactory, XMLInputFactory, or similar APIs without secure configuration (e.g., without disabling external entity resolution and DTD processing). Inspect application logs and incoming XML payloads for DOCTYPE and ENTITY definitions. Monitor for unexpected file access or outbound network requests during XML processing, especially when handling user-supplied XML. Implement automated scanning for XML payloads containing external entity references and alert on any file or network access patterns that deviate from normal application behavior.
